correctness.rationale: Homogeneity, exchange symmetry and the scale t=N(y)/N(x) reduce the arbitrary nonzero two-vector quotient to 0<=t<=1 and unit sphere u,v. For fixed t and p>=1, N(u+tv)^p+N(u-tv)^p is convex in both arguments on the product of two hexagon unit balls, so it attains its maximum at vertices. Inspecting six cyclic relative positions gives norm pairs (1+t,1-t),(1+t,1),(1,1+t),(1-t,1+t), hence exact upper and attained value 1+(1+t)^p. Independently checked all 36 vertex pairs at multiple distinct scales, including endpoints; this corroborates rather than replaces the symbolic six-position proof. The derivative of f_p(t) has sign H=t^(1-p)-(1+t)^(1-p)-1; for p>1 H strictly decreases from infinity to -2^(1-p), so the sole interior root is globally maximizing. The critical equation algebraically yields the displayed closed value. For p=1 f_1=(2+t)/(1+t), maximum 2 at t=0; for p=2 the golden-ratio result agrees with known prior exact value.

final_claim: For real Day–James hexagon N(s,t)=max(|s|,|t|,|s-t|), C_NJ^(1)=2 and for p>1 the all-p exact constant is ((1+tau_p)/(2tau_p))^(p-1), where the unique tau_p in (0,1) satisfies tau_p^(1-p)-(1+tau_p)^(1-p)=1; p=2 specializes to (3+sqrt5)/4.
